messages:
maria: Heads-up — we've been getting pagers for gpu-utilization spikes that are short-lived during nightly batch rollouts. I want to propose a change: only page when an allocation group's SLO is impacted for >10m, otherwise create a low-priority ticket. anyone object?
raj: +1 on intent. The current rule just pages on >85% for 3m which catches transient bursty jobs.
raj: Can we make it SLO-aware? e.g. if cluster_alloc_group in critical_slos -> page, else ticket.
tess: We should also group by alloc_group so one noisy tenant doesn't flood pages for the whole cluster. Grouping_key: alloc_group, cluster, node_pool.
maria: Agreed. Also want a mute window for rollout windows (00:00-05:00 in us-west) where we reduce paging sensitivity for non-critical allocs.
oliver: How about a two-tier Prometheus rule: alert gpu_utilization_warning (ticket) for 85% 3m, and gpu_utilization_breach (page) for 85% 10m AND slo_breached == 1. We can derive slo_breached with a recording rule.
raj: Example rule snippet I sketched:```yaml
- alert: GPUUtilizationPage
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization{job="node-exporter"}[10m]) > 0.85
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU util >85% for 10m"
- alert: GPUUtilizationTicket
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization{job="node-exporter"}[3m]) > 0.85
  labels:
    severity: ticket
  annotations:
    summary: "Transient GPU util spike (>85% 3m)"
```
maria: Nice. For the SLO check we can add a label on the alert via recording rule: `slo_impact{alloc_group=\"...\"}` which is 1 when p99 latency or error-rate SLOs are violated.
tess: Also we should set alert grouping in Alertmanager to `group_by: [\"cluster\",\"alloc_group\",\"severity\"]` and `group_wait`/`group_interval` to 30s/5m so repeated flares coalesce.
oliver: And add a dedupe window per alloc_group using `repeat_interval: 1h` for ticket-level alerts so we don't spam JIRA for the same tenant.
raj: For the mute windows: Alertmanager supports time_intervals. Example:```yaml
route:
  receiver: default-pager
  routes:
  - match:
      severity: ticket
    receiver: ticketing-endpoint
    mute_time_intervals: ["nightly-rollout"]
intervals:
  - name: "nightly-rollout"
    time_intervals:
      - times:
          - start_time: "00:00"
            end_time: "05:00"
            weekdays: [mon,tue,wed,thu,fri,sat,sun]
```
alert-bot: Deploy scheduled: alert-rule-update v1 will be applied at 2026-03-19T02:00Z to staging.
maria: Good. Let's run the rule in staging for 48h, measure paging->ticket ratios and false positives with the SLO-derived label.
raj: For telemetry, add two Grafana panels to the SLO dashboard: "Alerts by alloc_group (severity)" and "Pager-to-ticket ratio (7d)". Use PromQL: `count_over_time(ALERTS{alertname=~\"GPU.*\",severity=\"page\"}[7d]) / count_over_time(ALERTS{alertname=~\"GPU.*\"}[7d])`.
tess: Also log link in alert annotations: `dashboard_url` + `?var-cluster={{ $labels.cluster }}&var-alloc={{ $labels.alloc_group }}` so oncall can jump directly.
oliver: Ops checklist for the rollout: 1) apply rules in staging 2) run 48h eval 3) enable time_intervals in prod 4) monitor pager counts and SLO signals 5) revert if regressions.
maria: Quick Q: cost impact — will lowering paging sensitivity for non-critical allocs affect cost? it may slightly increase ticket triage but reduce paging ops. Anyone run numbers?
raj: We estimate ~20% fewer pages -> 0.5 FTE equivalent in ops saved annually. Ticket volume up ~10% but queued during day. Net $ is positive.
tess: I'll add a canned runbook entry: when GPUUtilizationPage fires, check `alloc_group`, `recent_deploys` label, and `slo_impact`. If slo_impact==0, escalate to ticket queue instead of paging.
alert-bot: Oncall rota notice: @oliver assigned night shift 2026-03-19 00:00-08:00 UTC.
maria: OK let's get the staging change up by EOD. I'll open a PR with the two-rule pattern + alertmanager route changes. Assigning follow-ups: @tess dashboard panel, @raj cost estimate, @oliver runbook update. :thumbsup:
oliver: ACK, will update runbook and add escalation play for critical alloc_group.
raj: ACK, will prepare the cost summary.
tess: ACK, will add panels and test dashboard links.
maria: Thanks team — we'll reconvene after the 48h staging run to decide prod flip.
